s0101.literal: Half of this year's field-rent tax was remitted in Bin-Di; Dongping's remission was three-tenths.
s0101.idiomatic: Half of this year's field rents in Bin-Di were remitted; Dongping's exemption was set at three-tenths.

s0102.literal: Ox relays were established from Yan to Kaiping; paper money was issued to purchase cart oxen.
s0102.idiomatic: Relay stations for draft oxen were set up from Yan to Kaiping, and notes were issued to buy cart cattle.

s0103.literal: On wuchen day, Left Grand Councillor Qur Qosa was made concurrent chief judicial officer of the Central Secretariat and granted a tiger tally.
s0103.idiomatic: On wuchen day Left Grand Councillor Qur Qosa was appointed concurrent chief judicial officer of the Secretariat and given a tiger tally.

s0104.literal: Locusts struck Zhending, Shuntian, and Xing prefectures.
s0104.idiomatic: Locusts plagued Zhending, Shuntian, and Xing.

s0105.literal: Sayid Ajall, Vice Grand Councillor, was also placed in charge of the Works Ministry and construction throughout the circuits; the foot-drawn crossbow Meng Lie presented was stored at the Central Capital.
s0105.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councillor Sayid Ajall was additionally put in charge of the Works Ministry and public works in every circuit; the powerful crossbow Meng Lie had submitted was stored at the Central Capital.

s0106.literal: On bingzi day, sea-eagle relays were established from Jinshan to Wangyun.
s0106.idiomatic: On bingzi day courier relays—the sea-eagle post—were opened from Jinshan to Wangyun.

s0107.literal: On dingchou day, Li Guoge and others were executed; Shi Tianze was ordered to select and assess the zongguan of Xu and Pi.
s0107.idiomatic: On dingchou day Li Guoge and his accomplices were executed, and Shi Tianze was ordered to choose and evaluate a new commander for Xu and Pi.

s0108.literal: On jiashen day, Bulaihaiya of Zhending Circuit had on his own authority executed three counterfeiters of paper notes; an edict inquired into his crime of violating regulations.
s0108.idiomatic: On jiashen day Bulaihaiya of Zhending circuit had summarily executed three makers of forged notes; an edict demanded an account of his breach of protocol.

s0109.literal: Frost at Xijing, Xuande, Weining, and Longmen; hail at Shuntian, Pingyang, Henan, and Zhending; drought at Dongping and Bin-Di.
s0109.idiomatic: Frost damaged crops at Xijing, Xuande, Weining, and Longmen; hail fell at Shuntian, Pingyang, Henan, and Zhending; Dongping and Bin-Di suffered drought.

s0110.literal: An edict ordered verification of fugitive households and of households paying silk-silver tax and rent; increase in registered population was to be rewarded and concealment punished; fugitive commoners who evaded corvée and taxes faced additional penalties.
s0110.idiomatic: An edict ordered a census of fugitive households and of those paying silk, silver, and land tax—growth in registered mouths was to be rewarded, concealment punished, and runaways who dodged levy and tax were to face heavier penalties still.

s0111.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture Yao Shu declined to go to the Secretariat for deliberations; the Emperor urged him to remain and ordered Shu and Liu Su, Minister of the Left Three Departments, to continue deliberating Secretariat affairs as before.
s0111.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Agriculture Yao Shu begged off attending Secretariat deliberations; Kublai pressed him to stay and told him and Liu Su, minister of the Left Three Departments, to keep handling Secretariat business as before.

s0112.literal: In the sixth month, on the yiyou new moon, Song troops attacked Cangzhou, Yazhou, and Lushan; the people had surrendered then rebelled again — seven ringleaders were ordered executed, the rest told to resume their livelihoods.
s0112.idiomatic: On the yiyou new moon of the sixth month Song forces struck Cangzhou, Yazhou, and Lushan. The populace had submitted and then risen again; seven chief instigators were put to death, the remainder ordered back to their occupations.

s0113.literal: Territory east of the Liao River was severed and placed under Kaiyuan Circuit.
s0113.idiomatic: Land east of the Liao River was detached and assigned to Kaiyuan circuit.

s0114.literal: On wuzi day, Han Shi'an, pacification commissioner of Bin-Di, defeated Song troops at the Dinghe mouth in Bin Prefecture.
s0114.idiomatic: On wuzi day Han Shi'an, pacification commissioner of Bin-Di, routed Song forces at the Dinghe estuary in Bin Prefecture.

s0115.literal: On jichou day, Tachar was dispatched to lead troops against the Song army and also to reassure coastal military and civilians.
s0115.idiomatic: On jichou day Tachar was sent at the head of an army against the Song and to pacify the coastal garrisons and people.

s0116.literal: On yiwei day, Jurchen encroachment on the people of Goryeo was forbidden; envoys traveling back and forth were to be escorted by officials.
s0116.idiomatic: On yiwei day Jurchen raids against Goryeo subjects were banned, and Goryeo envoys in transit were to be escorted by officials.

s0117.literal: The garrison-farm troops of Sapo Prefecture were moved west of the Yalu River to guard the sea route.
s0117.idiomatic: Sapo's garrison-farming troops were transferred west of the Yalu to watch the sea lanes.

s0118.literal: On bingshen day, King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent envoys bearing tribute.
s0118.idiomatic: On bingshen day King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent tribute envoys.

s0119.literal: On renyin day, the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported that artisan-soldiers at Xijing, Xuande, and Taiyuan were exhausted and asked that civilians replace them.
s0119.idiomatic: On renyin day the Shaanxi branch secretariat reported that artisan-troops at Xijing, Xuande, and Taiyuan were worn out and asked to substitute civilians in their place.

s0120.literal: An order stated: "Military registers are fixed and should not be disturbed; the rich and poor should support one another; those truly destitute may rest one year."
s0120.idiomatic: The court ordered: "Army rolls are set—do not disturb them. Let rich and poor aid each other; those in real want may stand down for a year."

s0121.literal: On guimao day, Li Yinuge, zongguan of Taiyuan, and the darughachi Daiquxue and others, having circulated Li Tan's forged proclamation through neighboring prefectures, were discovered and executed.
s0121.idiomatic: On guimao day Li Yinuge, commander of Taiyuan, and the darughachi Daiquxue and others—caught spreading Li Tan's forged summons through neighboring prefectures—were put to death.

s0122.literal: Ningwu Army was ordered to submit annually the iron it produced.
s0122.idiomatic: Ningwu Army was ordered to deliver its iron output to the state each year.

s0123.literal: Civilians in Hexi and soldiers under Prince Husaji lacked food; paper money was issued for relief.
s0123.idiomatic: People in Hexi and soldiers of Prince Husaji's command were starving; notes were issued for famine relief.

s0124.literal: On renzi day, the prohibition on military officers and soldiers harassing civilians was strictly enforced.
s0124.idiomatic: On renzi day the ban on officers and troops molesting civilians was sharply reinforced.

s0125.literal: On guichou day, four ironworks were established at Xiaoyu, Luzi, Ningwu Army, and Chiniquan.
s0125.idiomatic: On guichou day ironworks were opened at Xiaoyu, Luzi, Ningwu Army, and Chiniquan.

s0126.literal: Yan Zhongji of Dongping had borrowed from the people money to pay taxes totaling 437,400 ingots, and had also borrowed more than 15,000 taels of silver from revenue, note capital, and salt levy; an edict ordered these not collected.
s0126.idiomatic: Yan Zhongji of Dongping had raised 437,400 ingots in taxes by borrowing from the populace and had drawn more than 15,000 taels of silver from revenue, note reserves, and the salt tax; an edict remitted all of it.

s0127.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on wuwu day, corvée and tax obligations were restored for Mongol army relay households; the lump-sum silver payment of peasant households was halved; captive households were required to pay only silk; in months when people owed taxes, private debts were not to be collected.
s0127.idiomatic: On wuwu day in the seventh month of autumn corvée and taxes were restored for Mongol relay households; peasants' lump-sum silver dues were cut in half; captive households owed only silk; and in tax months private debts could not be collected.

s0128.literal: For gold and silver sold on the private market, payment was to be reckoned in paper notes only.
s0128.idiomatic: Private trade in gold and silver was to be settled in notes alone.

s0129.literal: On bingyin day, Yang Dayuan of the Qizhou Branch Secretariat was granted ten gold tally tokens and nineteen silver tally tokens to reward the officers and soldiers under his command;
s0129.idiomatic: On bingyin day Yang Dayuan of the Qizhou branch secretariat received ten gold tallies and nineteen silver tallies to reward his officers and men;

s0130.literal: two sea-eagle tally tokens were separately granted — for urgent matters one might ride post-haste to report upward.
s0130.idiomatic: two sea-eagle tallies besides, so that urgent reports could be rushed up the chain by relay.

s0131.literal: A relay was established at Qianggan Ridge to facilitate transport.
s0131.idiomatic: A relay station was opened at Qianggan Ridge to speed supply runs.

s0132.literal: On guiyou day, Gan Prefecture suffered famine; silver was issued for relief.
s0132.idiomatic: On guiyou day Gan Prefecture was starving; silver was sent for relief.

s0133.literal: On jiaxu day, Li Tan, hard pressed, entered Daming Lake; he threw himself into the water but did not die immediately; he was captured, and the Mongol soldier Nangia was executed with him; their bodies were dismembered and displayed as a warning.
s0133.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Li Tan, driven to the wall, fled into Daming Lake and threw himself into the water but did not drown at once. He was taken alive; the Mongol soldier Nangia was executed with him, and both corpses were cut apart and paraded as a warning.

s0134.literal: On wuyin day, Liu Zheng of the Kuifu Branch Secretariat was put in charge of the Central Secretariat for Chengdu and Tongchuan circuits; ten thousand taels of silver were also granted and distributed to soldiers who had lost their livelihood.
s0134.idiomatic: On wuyin day Liu Zheng of the Kuifu branch secretariat was made acting head of the Secretariat for Chengdu and Tongchuan; ten thousand taels of silver were also granted and paid out to soldiers left without livelihood.

s0135.literal: In the eighth month, on jichou day, Guo Shoujing requested opening Jade Spring to connect the grain transport; Wang Yunzhong of the Guangji River and Canal Office requested opening the Zhang, Fu, Li rivers and Da Spring in Xing, Ming, and elsewhere to irrigate farmland — both were approved.
s0135.idiomatic: On jichou day in the eighth month Guo Shoujing asked to tap Jade Spring for the grain route; Wang Yunzhong of the Guangji river-and-canal office asked to open the Zhang, Fu, Li, and Da Spring in Xing, Ming, and neighboring districts to water farmlands—both requests were granted.

s0136.literal: On jiawu day, Bodughan and others memorialized requesting that silver mines at Xuande Prefecture, Dexing Prefecture, and elsewhere be entrusted to artisan households, with silver, malachite, and cinnabar submitted annually to the government — approved.
s0136.idiomatic: On jiawu day Bodughan and others asked that the Xuande and Dexing silver works be turned over to registered artisan households, delivering silver, malachite, and vermilion to the state each year—the court agreed.

s0137.literal: On bingwu day, medical instructors were established in all circuits.
s0137.idiomatic: On bingwu day instructors of medicine were appointed in every circuit.

s0138.literal: On wushen day, Wang E was ordered to gather court ministers to discuss historical matters; E and others requested that records of the previous reign be deposited with the History Office.
s0138.idiomatic: On wushen day Wang E was told to assemble ministers to debate historical matters; he and his colleagues asked that materials on the prior reign be turned over to the historiography office.

s0139.literal: Frost fell and damaged crops in Hejian, Pingluan, Guangning, Xijing, Xuande, and Beijing.
s0139.idiomatic: Killing frost struck Hejian, Pingluan, Guangning, Xijing, Xuande, and Beijing.

s0140.literal: In the ninth month, on wuwu day, Zhang Honglue, wanhu of Bozhou, defeated Song troops at Qi County and recovered Su and Qi.
s0140.idiomatic: On wuwu day in the ninth month Zhang Honglue, wanhu of Bozhou, broke Song forces at Qi County and retook Su and Qi.

s0141.literal: Dong Wenbing, commander of the Imperial Guard, was made concurrent Eastern Shandong Military Commissioner; old troops of Yidu were gathered as the Wuwei Guard to garrison the south; an edict ordered Grand Governor Sagis of the Yidu Branch Secretariat and Dong Wenbing to confer on military and civilian registers — of every ten households only two were to serve in the Wuwei Guard;
s0141.idiomatic: Dong Wenbing, commander of the Imperial Guard, was also named military commissioner of eastern Shandong; surviving Yidu troops were mustered into the Wuwei guard for frontier duty. Sagis, grand governor of the Yidu branch secretariat, and Dong Wenbing were ordered to sort military and civilian registers—two households in ten were to be taken for the Wuwei guard;

s0142.literal: those transferred from Haizhou, Donghai, and Lianshui into Yidu were also placed under this guard.
s0142.idiomatic: transfers from Haizhou, Donghai, and Lianshui into Yidu were placed under the same command.

s0143.literal: On jiwei day, the sea-eagle relay at Bazhou was abolished.
s0143.idiomatic: On jiwei day the sea-eagle relay at Bazhou was shut down.

s0144.literal: Tran Quang Binh of Annam sent envoys bearing tribute goods.
s0144.idiomatic: Tran Quang Binh of Annam sent envoys with tribute goods.

s0145.literal: On renxu day, Xing Prefecture was renamed Shunde Prefecture and a pacification commission was established; Ming, Ci, and Wei prefectures were placed under it.
s0145.idiomatic: On renxu day Xing Prefecture was raised to Shunde Prefecture with a pacification office; Ming, Ci, and Wei were attached to it.

s0146.literal: The people of Taiyuan were permitted to consume small salt, paying seven thousand five hundred taels of silver annually.
s0146.idiomatic: Taiyuan people were allowed to use petty salt on payment of seven thousand five hundred taels of silver a year.

s0147.literal: On jisi day, for supplying the army, Ma Yuehenai was appointed Minister of Rites and granted a gold tally token.
s0147.idiomatic: On jisi day Ma Yuehenai, rewarded for provisioning the army, was made minister of rites and given a gold tally.

s0148.literal: On renshen day, King Tran Quang Binh of Annam and the darughachi Nala Ding were granted tiger tallies.
s0148.idiomatic: On renshen day King Tran Quang Binh of Annam and the darughachi Nala Ding received tiger tallies.

s0149.literal: Jinan officials were ordered: all public and private arrears owed by military and civilians were temporarily suspended from collection.
s0149.idiomatic: Jinan officials were told to hold in abeyance every public and private debt owed by soldiers and civilians.

s0150.literal: On guiyou day, Grand Commander Köke Temür died in camp; his elder brother Aju was appointed in his stead, granted a tiger tally, and placed in command of Mongol and Han troops on the southern front.
s0150.idiomatic: On guiyou day Grand Commander Köke Temür died on campaign; his elder brother Aju replaced him, received a tiger tally, and took command of Mongol and Han forces on the southern front.

s0151.literal: On the jiashen new moon of the intercalary month, Sha and Su prefectures lacked food; rice and paper money were issued for relief.
s0151.idiomatic: On the jiashen new moon of the intercalary month Sha and Su ran short of grain; rice and notes were issued for relief.

s0152.literal: On dinghai day, a relay was established at Gubeikou.
s0152.idiomatic: On dinghai day a relay was opened at Gubeikou.

s0153.literal: On jichou day, the people of Jinan were starving; their taxes were remitted.
s0153.idiomatic: On jichou day Jinan was famine-struck; taxes there were remitted.

s0154.literal: Other corvée obligations for military households throughout the circuits were remitted.
s0154.idiomatic: All other levy duties on military households in every circuit were waived.

s0155.literal: On gengyin day, an order established six relays from Shun Prefecture in the capital region to Kaiping.
s0155.idiomatic: On gengyin day six relay stations were set between Shun Prefecture in the capital region and Kaiping.

s0156.literal: On xinmao day, Yan Zhongfan memorialized requesting to fill posts for temple-school and Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians in Dongping Circuit — approved.
s0156.idiomatic: On xinmao day Yan Zhongfan asked to fill vacancies for temple-school and imperial-sacrifice musicians in Dongping circuit—the request was granted.

s0157.literal: The Wuwei Guard and the Black Army were ordered to assemble at the capital.
s0157.idiomatic: The Wuwei guard and the Black Army were ordered to muster at the capital.

s0158.literal: On gengzi day, Jiuzhu, qianhu of the Middle Wing, defeated Song troops at Hunao Mountain.
s0158.idiomatic: On gengzi day Jiuzhu, qianhu of the middle wing, routed Song troops at Hunao Mountain.

s0159.literal: On gengxu day, three hundred thousand shi of grain was issued to relieve the starving people of Jinan.
s0159.idiomatic: On gengxu day three hundred thousand shi of grain was opened to feed Jinan's hungry.

s0160.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on bingchen day, two thousand garrison soldiers at Jin Prefecture and newly drafted wall-defense troops of Daming and Henan were released to civilian status.
s0160.idiomatic: On bingchen day in the tenth month of winter two thousand troops garrisoning Jin Prefecture and newly levied wall-guards of Daming and Henan were mustered out as civilians.

s0161.literal: On gengshen day, Yidu's military and civilians were split in two — Dong Wenbing led the army, Sagis governed the people.
s0161.idiomatic: On gengshen day Yidu's soldiers and civilians were divided: Dong Wenbing took the army, Sagis the civil administration.

s0162.literal: Princes, envoys, and armies who dared rely on their power to harass civilians were to be seized wherever found and reported.
s0162.idiomatic: Any prince, envoy, or army that used its standing to bully the people was to be arrested on the spot and reported.

s0163.literal: An edict ordered horses Li Tan had plundered from civilians returned to their owners.
s0163.idiomatic: An edict commanded that horses Li Tan had seized from the people be returned to their owners.

s0164.literal: Because Hao Jing and Liu Renjie, envoys to Song, had not returned, their families were granted grain stipends.
s0164.idiomatic: Because Hao Jing and Liu Renjie, still abroad as envoys to Song, had not come back, their households were put on official grain allowance.

s0165.literal: The Secretariat memorialized proposing trade with Song to stop private merchants, restore fugitive civilians trapped in Song, and reconnoiter Lian and Hai prefectures — not approved.
s0165.idiomatic: The Secretariat proposed opening trade with Song to choke off smugglers, bring home subjects trapped in Song territory, and scout Lian and Hai—the request was denied.

s0166.literal: Because Liu Renjie had not joined Li Tan, he was promoted to zongguan of Yidu Circuit and granted gold and silk.
s0166.idiomatic: Liu Renjie, who had refused to follow Li Tan, was promoted to commander of Yidu circuit and rewarded with gold and silk.

s0167.literal: On renxu day, seventeen gold tally tokens and eleven silver tally tokens were granted to officials of prefectures and counties under the Grand Governorate of the Yidu Branch Secretariat.
s0167.idiomatic: On renxu day seventeen gold tallies and eleven silver tallies were issued to prefectural and county officers under the Yidu branch secretariat's grand governorship.

s0168.literal: On yichou day, an edict forbade hunting in the capital region.
s0168.idiomatic: On yichou day hunting in the capital region was banned.

s0169.literal: On bingyin day, the Eastern and Western Sichuan grand command headquarters were split in two; Tede and Liu Zheng and others were made grand commanders and left and right deputy grand commanders.
s0169.idiomatic: On bingyin day the eastern and western Sichuan grand marshals' offices were divided in two; Tede, Liu Zheng, and others were named grand marshals and left and right deputies.

s0170.literal: An edict rebuked Goryeo for disrespect.
s0170.idiomatic: An edict rebuked Goryeo for arrogance and slights.

s0171.literal: Another edict granted King Wang Chon of Goryeo an official calendar.
s0171.idiomatic: Another edict presented King Wang Chon of Goryeo with the reign calendar.

s0172.literal: For military merit, Wang Zhang, darughachi of Qu Prefecture, and others were rewarded fifty taels of gold and 1,550 taels of silver.
s0172.idiomatic: Wang Zhang, darughachi of Qu Prefecture, and others were rewarded for battle honors with fifty taels of gold and 1,550 taels of silver.

s0173.literal: Five thousand taels of silver were granted for military merit at He Prefecture under the grand commander of Lang and Peng circuits.
s0173.idiomatic: Five thousand taels of silver were granted for feats at He Prefecture under the grand marshal of Lang and Peng circuits.

s0174.literal: On dingmao day, an edict placed Fengxiang Prefecture's garrison-farm troops under military registers while continuing to farm at Fengxiang.
s0174.idiomatic: On dingmao day an edict enrolled Fengxiang's garrison-farming troops in the army rolls while keeping them on the land at Fengxiang.

s0175.literal: Nine hundred fifteen troops drafted by Diao Guoqi in Pingyang Army were released to civilian status.
s0175.idiomatic: Nine hundred fifteen men levied by Diao Guoqi in Pingyang Army were discharged to civilian life.

s0176.literal: Qincha, grand commander of Lang, Peng, Guang'an, Shunqing, Kuifu, and other circuits, garrisoned Qingju Mountain and requested reinforcements; the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and Wang Weizheng, commander of Gongchang, were ordered to augment him with troops.
s0176.idiomatic: Qincha, grand marshal of Lang, Peng, Guang'an, Shunqing, Kuifu, and neighboring circuits, held Qingju Mountain and asked for more men; the Shaanxi branch secretariat and Wang Weizheng of Gongchang were ordered to send reinforcements.

s0177.literal: On wuchen day, Yang Dayuan requested to exchange salt for army grain at Da'an Army in Li Prefecture — approved.
s0177.idiomatic: On wuchen day Yang Dayuan asked to trade salt for rations at Da'an Army in Li Prefecture—the request was granted.

s0178.literal: On gengwu day, Wang Weizheng, commander of Gongchang, was ordered to bring back the garrison at Qingju and farm at Li Prefecture.
s0178.idiomatic: On gengwu day Wang Weizheng of Gongchang was told to withdraw the Qingju garrison and put the men to farming in Li Prefecture.

s0179.literal: On yihai day, the Left and Right Sections of the Central Secretariat were divided.
s0179.idiomatic: On yihai day the Secretariat was split into left and right departments.

s0180.literal: On dingchou day, an order directed the eight Song captives Wang Yong, Xia Zhen, and others taken by Wang Da and other baihu of Suzhou to be sent to the capital.
s0180.idiomatic: On dingchou day an order sent to the capital the eight Song prisoners—Wang Yong, Xia Zhen, and the rest—seized by Wang Da and fellow centurions of Suzhou.

s0181.literal: The hostage-army led by Baijanu was ordered to enter court service.
s0181.idiomatic: The hostage corps under Baijanu was ordered into palace service.

s0182.literal: On wuyin day, the hostage-armies of Gu'an and Pingluan under Bulila were ordered to move back from Yidu to their original lands.
s0182.idiomatic: On wuyin day the Gu'an and Pingluan hostage troops under Bulila were ordered home from Yidu to their old stations.

s0183.literal: An edict pardoned all officials, soldiers, and civilians of Yidu Prefecture Circuit who had followed Li Tan under coercion.
s0183.idiomatic: An edict pardoned every Yidu official, soldier, and commoner who had marched with Li Tan under duress.

s0184.literal: Wanhu Yan Zhongfan was ordered to restore Su Prefecture and Qi County; wanhu Huduhu, Huaidu, and Commander He were ordered to complete the walls of Pi Prefecture.
s0184.idiomatic: Wanhu Yan Zhongfan was charged with rebuilding Su Prefecture and Qi County; wanhu Huduhu, Huaidu, and Commander He with finishing the walls of Pi Prefecture.

s0185.literal: In the eleventh month, on yiyou day, Venus transited the Hook and Flail asterism.
s0185.idiomatic: On yiyou day in the eleventh month Venus crossed the Hook and Flail.

s0186.literal: On dinghai day, an order directed Shengan Temple to hold the Buddha-Crown Golden Wheel Assembly and Changchun Palace to set up the Golden Register Universal Heaven Ritual.
s0186.idiomatic: On dinghai day Shengan Temple was ordered to hold the Buddha-Crown Golden Wheel rite and Changchun Palace to perform the Golden Register ritual for All under Heaven.

s0187.literal: On xinchou day, the sun showed a counter-glow with a triple halo and three mock suns.
s0187.idiomatic: On xinchou day the sun showed a counter-glow, a heavy triple halo, and three attendant disks.

s0188.literal: Jinan people whose goods had been plundered by Li Tan's officers were ordered to bring suits before Grand Governor Sagis.
s0188.idiomatic: Jinan people robbed by Li Tan's lieutenants were told to bring their claims before Grand Governor Sagis.

s0189.literal: The Zhending commoner Hao Xing killed Ma Zhong in revenge; Zhong's son Rong accepted silver from Xing and had Xing take his place in military service.
s0189.idiomatic: At Zhending the commoner Hao Xing killed Ma Zhong to avenge a grudge; Zhong's son Rong took silver from Xing and let Xing stand in for his army duty.

s0190.literal: The Secretariat judged Rong for taking bribes and forgetting his feud — unworthy of a son — flogged him and confiscated the silver.
s0190.idiomatic: The Secretariat ruled that Rong, bought off and forgetful of vengeance, had failed the duty of a son; he was flogged and the silver forfeited.

s0191.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict affirmed the judgment according to law.
s0191.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, an edict upheld the sentence as lawful.

s0192.literal: The crime of the officials' leniency in sentencing was referred to the Secretariat for deliberation.
s0192.idiomatic: The local officers' offense of undue leniency was left to the Secretariat to decide.

s0193.literal: Salt-pan households at Sanchagou, burned and plundered by Song troops, were exempted from this year's rent and taxes.
s0193.idiomatic: Salt-boiler households at Sanchagou, burned and looted by Song troops, were excused this year's rent and tax.

s0194.literal: Artisans of the Palace Workshop Directorate were culled; the skilled among them, twelve hundred households, were retained.
s0194.idiomatic: Craftsmen of the palace workshops were thinned out; the able twelve hundred households were kept.

s0195.literal: Officials were dispatched to review serious criminal cases in Shaanxi.
s0195.idiomatic: Commissioners were sent to hear capital and other grave cases in Shaanxi.

s0196.literal: Hexi people migrating to Ying Prefecture: one hundred sixty households unable to support themselves were given oxen, tools, and millet and wheat seed; cloth was also granted, two bolts per person.
s0196.idiomatic: Among Hexi people resettled in Ying Prefecture, one hundred sixty destitute households received oxen, tools, and millet and wheat seed; each person was also given two bolts of cloth.

s0197.literal: On yisi day, an edict ordered Grand Commander Aju to divide out three thousand troops together with the forces of Axiambuhua and Huaidu to re-establish Su Prefecture, Qi County, and Pi Prefecture.
s0197.idiomatic: On yisi day an edict told Grand Commander Aju to detach three thousand men, join the forces of Axiambuhua and Huaidu, and reestablish Su Prefecture, Qi County, and Pi Prefecture.

s0198.literal: An order instructed Shi Tianze: "If I act in anger and wish to execute someone, you should delay one or two days and submit a memorial before carrying it out."
s0198.idiomatic: Kublai instructed Shi Tianze: "When anger moves me to kill, hold the order a day or two and memorialise back before you act."

s0199.literal: On bingwu day, an edict for specially recruited personnel ordered that they travel by relay courier.
s0199.idiomatic: On bingwu day an edict on special recruitment ordered that appointees travel by official relay.

s0200.literal: On wushen day, Fu Prefecture was promoted to Longxing Prefecture, with Sirag'otu as zongguan; Huai'an and Tiancheng of Xuande and Weining and Gaoyuan were severed and placed under it.
s0200.idiomatic: On wushen day Fu Prefecture was raised to Longxing Prefecture under Sirag'otu; Huai'an and Tiancheng of Xuande and Weining and Gaoyuan were cut away and attached to it.
